title: Define response-envelope SLOs and progressive-release acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers integrating hosted and dedicated inference endpoints have reported opaque failure modes when partial responses are returned (e.g., early stream termination, truncated envelope metadata). We need a clear operational contract — a response-envelope SLO — that defines per-endpoint latency bands for initial token, first meaningful byte, and final completion; an error budget formulation for truncated/partial responses; and explicit staged rollout gates that block model or runtime changes when burn rates exceed thresholds. Goals: 1) Produce a concise PRD that specifies measurable SLO targets across product tiers and deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private). 2) Define error budget calculation for truncated or malformed envelopes and map to automated canary/rollback rules. 3) Produce per-stage acceptance criteria and checklist for Console gating (dashboards, alert rules, smoke tests). Scope clarifications: - This ticket covers SLO definition, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating only. It does not include implementing instrumentation or enforcement logic (ENG owners). - Include both streaming chat and non-streaming generation; for embeddings we will reference separate embedding SLO ticket. - Per-tenant SLOs are out of scope for initial rollout but include notes/proposal for later iteration. Out-of-scope: complete infra implementation, private on-prem installability constraints, license changes. Deliverables: 1) PRD document (Confluence link) with tables of latency targets and error budget definitions; 2) Canonical rollout checklist that Console and SRE can consume; 3) Set of contract tests (description) that ENG will implement in a follow-up engineering ticket.
acceptance_criteria: SLO table exists with p50/p95/p99 targets for three observability checkpoints: time-to-first-token, time-to-first-meaningful-byte (FMB), time-to-final-token for hosted, dedicated, and private; targets differentiated by workload class (interactive chat, batch completions)
Error budget definition documents how truncated or malformed response-envelopes count against the budget and how partial/streamed failures are classified (hard-failure vs degradations)
Burn-rate thresholds and canary gates defined: canary pass if no metric breaches; progressive traffic increase stops if 5-minute burn-rate > 2x baseline for critical endpoints

Rollout checklist created for Console that includes required dashboards, alerting rules (SRE-runbook links), and automated smoke tests (first-token, FMB, final-token), with clear owners and required sign-offs
Acceptance tests enumerated and mapped to follow-up ENG tickets (tests include synthetic latency injection, truncated-payload simulator, and end-to-end contract tests against model variants)
Communication plan for customers (status page and customer-facing SLA note) drafted and linked in PRD
PRD reviewed and approved by SRE, Runtime ENG lead, and Design for error-state UX messaging; approvals recorded in ticket comments
notes: 11/10: Initial scoping: PM, Runtime ENG, SRE sync — agreed to canonicalize on three checkpoints rather than arbitrary token counts to simplify instrumentation.
11/13: Decision: Use percentage-of-requests basis for error budget (rather than token-weighted) for first rollout to keep calculations tractable for Console and billing alignment.
11/16: Trade-off discussion: per-tenant SLOs would provide finer guarantees but add significant rollout complexity; flagged as v2 (see proposal section in PRD).
11/18: Runtime ENG recommends including an explicit compatibility matrix for quantized model variants — impacts p99 tail; added as appendix to PRD.
11/20: SRE pushed back on 95th percentile gating for canary because short windows amplify noise; compromise: require both 5m burn-rate and stable 1h p95 trend before advancing traffic fraction.
11/22: Added acceptance checklist items for UI copy that explains degraded responses to end-users (Design owner: Mara Kim).
11/24: PM review complete — ready for cross-functional approval meeting scheduled 2025-11-26.
